overview.headline: Newton laws linking motion, mass, force and reaction

keyPoints.point: object remains in motion at constant speed when external forces cancel
keyPoints.quote: An object at rest remains at rest, and an object in motion remains in motion at constant speed

keyPoints.point: acceleration depends on mass and amount of force applied to an object
keyPoints.quote: The acceleration of an object depends on the mass of the object and the amount of force applied.

keyPoints.point: mass times velocity defines momentum for an object in motion
keyPoints.quote: Momentum is defined to be the mass m of an object times its velocity V.

keyPoints.point: action forces have an equal and opposite reaction in nature
keyPoints.quote: His third law states that for every action (force) in nature there is an equal and opposite reaction.

keyTerms.gloss: tendency to resist changes in motion state
keyTerms.quote: This tendency to resist changes in a state of motion is inertia.

keyTerms.gloss: mass times velocity of moving object
keyTerms.quote: Momentum is defined to be the mass m of an object times its velocity V.

keyTerms.gloss: change caused by applied force on mass
keyTerms.quote: The acceleration of an object depends on the mass of the object and the amount of force applied.

keyTerms.gloss: total force acting on an object to keep velocity
keyTerms.quote: If there is no net force acting on the object, then the object will maintain a constant velocity.

keyTerms.gloss: quantity with magnitude and direction scientists call vector
keyTerms.quote: Scientists and mathematicians call this a vector quantity.
